objective: Refuse at intake any proposal filed at est_core_min zero that carries no explicit justification for the zero, and require the cost basis alongside it, because the ranking denominator is arithmetically inert on half the closed docket and the scorecard measured that an estimate's provenance predicts its accuracy better than its value does
rationale: This is filed as the remedy for a defect the EIG lookback found while testing something else, and the defect is a filing defect rather than a ranking defect, which is why it is fixed at intake rather than argued about as a weight. Of the 114 closed docket items, 52 were filed at est_core_min zero and 54 sit at or below the ranking's 1.0 core-minute floor, so on 47 percent of the closed record the division in rank_value does nothing at all and the control room's label, expected knowledge gain per core minute deterministic, describes a quantity that is just the numerator. Both candidate rankings tested in the lookback inherit that, so no choice of numerator repairs it. The lookback also measured that where the denominator does differentiate it points the wrong way: ranking by cost most-expensive-first correlates with delivered value at rho +0.282 with p 0.002 and a top-20 precision of 0.70, beating both the incumbent heuristic and the EIG composite on every metric in the comparison. A denominator that is inert on half the docket and inverted on the rest is not a weighting problem. The second half of the requirement comes from the calibration scorecard's sharpest measured finding, which is that the predictor is the basis and not a factor: estimates anchored on a measured sibling missed by at most 1.84 times, while unanchored forecasts ran to 13.55 times and are the entire tail in both directions. A zero that is zero because the work is arithmetic over records already on disk is a measured zero and is worth trusting; a zero that is zero because nobody priced it is a blank, and today the two are indistinguishable at intake and identical in the ranking. The refusal asks for the difference to be stated. Precedent exists and is close: the cost-basis refusal already refuses a basis that cites a superseded run and caught three docket entries doing exactly that, and the refused-bases list keeps refusals visible so a refusal is never a silent drop. This extends that machinery by one clause rather than inventing any. Axis A: capability-kind at zero solver cost. Axis B: 0. Axis C: 0.

cost_basis: measured; the refusal is one clause beside intake checks that already exist and already refuse a cost basis, the affected population is a count over the docket, and the retrospective is arithmetic over records on disk
expected_knowledge_gain: Two outcomes, and the second is the one worth filing for. One: the refusal lands and every future zero-cost filing states why it is free, which makes the ranking denominator mean something for the first time and lets the per-core-min language on the control room surface be either defended or retired on evidence. Two: the retrospective the refusal forces over the 52 existing zero-priced items finds that a large share of them are not measured zeros at all but unpriced blanks, which would say that the docket has been ranking half its own work on a number nobody ever stated, and would be the same class of defect as the gain table's silent 2.0 default that ranked 24 of 55 proposals before it was caught. Either way the lab learns whether zero has been a measurement or a shrug.
in_sample_verdict: Not applicable. Nothing is fitted, inverted or calibrated, no test data is read, no model is trained and no scored column moves. The item adds a refusal at intake and counts an existing population.
sequencing: Dispatchable now, zero solver cost, Infra family. Existing entries are grandfathered where they stand, on the SCHEMA_REQUIRED_FROM precedent: the docket's existing rows are never rewritten and never refused retroactively, they only stop being the pattern for new ones. The retrospective count over the 52 is a report, not a rewrite.
gate: Intake refuses a proposal created from the adoption date that carries est_core_min zero without a justification field, and refuses one that carries no cost_basis, with both refusals surfaced the way the refused-bases list already surfaces its own rather than dropped silently. A test proves the refusal fires and proves a justified zero passes. Separately, a count over the 52 existing zero-priced closed items classifies each as a measured zero or an unpriced blank against its own cost_basis text, and that count is published whatever it says.
